items.q: A patient with a midline neck swelling undergoes Technetium-99m (Tc^99m) scintigraphy. The scan demonstrates no uptake in the normal anatomical location and prominent uptake in an abnormal subhyoid region. What is the diagnosis?
opts: Toxic adenoma of the left lobe
items.exp: The scintigraphy image on page 903 shows a Tc-99m scan of ectopic thyroid, with 'No uptake in normal location' and 'Uptake in ectopic location'. (Book p903)

items.q: Match the thyroid disorder to its effect on the Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) — 1) Hypothyroidism 2) Hyperthyroidism … A) Decreased (↓) BMR B) Increased (↑) BMR
items.exp: Thyroid hormone maintains BMR: hypothyroidism leads to decreased BMR, whereas hyperthyroidism causes increased BMR. (Book p903)

items.q: Which receptor family is explicitly listed under 'Cardiac actions' of thyroid hormone on page 903?
items.exp: Page 903 explicitly notes: 'Cardiac actions (α-receptors): ↑ Cardiac output (CO), ↑ O2 utilization, ↑ heart rate'. (Book p903)

items.q: Thyroid hormone stimulates tissue oxygen (O2) utilization throughout the body, with the explicit exception of the ___ and ___.
items.exp: Thyroid hormone causes increased O2 utilization '(Except brain & gonads)'. (Book p903)

items.q: Regarding the vascular and hemodynamic effects on page 903: I Toxicosis leads directly to increased cardiac output (CO). II Hyperthyroidism increases peripheral resistance, leading to increased blood pressure (BP).
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Page 903 notes: 'Toxicosis -> ↑ CO' and 'Hyperthyroidism -> ↑ peripheral resistance -> ↑ BP'. (Book p903)

items.q: Thyroid hormone drives thermogenesis by acting as an uncoupler of ___; a severe deficiency in myxedema coma causes ___.
opts: The citric acid cycle; heat stroke
items.exp: Thyroid hormone acts as an uncoupler of oxidative phosphorylation producing thermogenesis; its lack in myxedema coma results in hypothermia. (Book p903)

items.q: What two key effects of thyroid hormone on carbohydrate metabolism are outlined on page 903?
opts: Gluconeogenesis stimulation and glucose uptake into cells (with insulin resistance in hypothyroidism)
Glycogen synthesis stimulation and peripheral insulin sensitization
Direct inhibition of hepatic glucokinase and activation of intestinal SGLT-1
Suppression of pancreatic glucagon release and acceleration of glycolysis
items.exp: In carbohydrate metabolism, thyroid hormone drives: 1. Gluconeogenesis, and 2. Glucose uptake into cells (with hypothyroidism predisposing to insulin resistance). (Book p903)

items.q: Regarding fat metabolism: I Thyroid hormone causes minimal lipolysis. II Thyroid hormone stimulates cholesterol clearance; therefore, hypothyroidism results in hypercholesterolemia.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Under fat metabolism: 1. Lipolysis (minimal), 2. Cholesterol clearance (Hypothyroidism : Hypercholesterolemia). (Book p903)

items.q: A patient with severe long-standing thyrotoxicosis develops proximal muscle wasting, osteopenia with pathological fractures, and hypercalcemia with nephrolithiasis. What catabolic mechanism explains these findings?
opts: Potent catabolic proteolysis causing myopathy, osteopenia/osteoporosis, and hypercalcemia leading to hypercalciuria and stones
Severe uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation causing muscular lactic acidosis and stone deposition
Enhanced gluconeogenesis depleting muscle glycogen and causing secondary hyperparathyroidism
Impaired cholesterol clearance inducing osteoclast atheromatous emboli
items.exp: In significant toxicosis, thyroid hormone acts as a potent catabolic hormone driving proteolysis -> myopathy, osteopenia -> osteoporosis, and hypercalcemia -> hypercalciuria -> stones. (Book p903)

items.q: Match the physiological action of thyroid hormone to its target organ — 1) CNS 2) Vitamin metabolism 3) Bone marrow … A) Myelination B) β-Carotene conversion to Vitamin A C) Stimulates erythropoiesis
items.exp: Thyroid hormone promotes myelination of the CNS, converts beta-carotene to vitamin A, and stimulates erythropoiesis in bone marrow. (Book p903)

items.q: Why can hypothyroid patients exhibit yellowish-orange skin discoloration while sparing the sclerae?
opts: Impaired conversion of β-carotene to Vitamin A leads to carotenemia
Extensive accumulation of glycosaminoglycans in the sclerae
Accelerated breakdown of red blood cells from erythropoietic arrest
items.exp: Thyroid hormone is responsible for converting beta-carotene to vitamin A; in hypothyroidism this conversion is impaired, leading to hypercarotenemia and yellowing of skin. (Book p903)

items.q: Thyroid hormone maintains reproductive fertility; the sequential menstrual derangement noted in untreated hypothyroidism is: menorrhagia → ___ → infertility.
items.exp: Under fertility maintenance: 'Hypothyroidism -> menorrhagia -> Oligo/amenorrhea -> Infertility'. (Book p903)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed on page 903 as a physiologic function or target of thyroid hormone?
opts: Inhibition of erythropoiesis in bone marrow
Myelination of the central nervous system
Conversion of β-carotene to vitamin A
items.exp: Thyroid hormone stimulates erythropoiesis, not inhibits it. It also maintains BMR, promotes CNS myelination, and converts beta-carotene to vitamin A. (Book p903)
